$comment: VERSIONED CONTENT, NOT CODE (hard rule 14). The words of the messages this platform sends a PATIENT about their own portal record. They live here rather than inline in a dispatcher for the same reason the enduring termination notice does: this regime moved twice and reversed once, copy must be editable without a code change, and the version must travel with every message produced from it. THE RECORD ID LINE IS ITS OWN TEMPLATE because it appears in every portal-related message, not only the invitation -- one set of words appended by one helper, so a patient comparing two messages sees the same sentence both times. That sameness IS the anti-scam check (Carl, 4 Sep 2026): a page, a passkey and a message all quoting one id. WHAT THESE WORDS MAY NEVER SAY. No benefit and no dollar amount of any kind (hard rule 4) -- reg 89AA notices are the one place an amount belongs and they are a different document. Never 'certified', 'approved', 'accredited' or 'government-approved' (hard rule 12, REQ-65C-05). Never a Medicare card number, which is not an identity identifier and is not held here at all (hard rule 1, REQ-VER-02). Never a suggestion that care, an appointment or billing depends on opening the portal -- it never does (hard rule 8; REQ-PORT-08: portal access is never a precondition of signing). PLACEHOLDERS ARE KEYS, NEVER VALUES. A name, a practice name and a link are substituted at send time; nothing personal is written into this file. UK/AU spelling and plain language, because the audience is every patient rather than a confident one.

templates.note: FR-1.14 -- the offer of portal activation, made after a completed signature and never before. It is an OFFER: the second paragraph says plainly that nothing depends on accepting it.
templates.subject: See your bulk-billing record with {{practiceName}}
paragraphs: {{practiceName}} has offered you a way to see your own bulk-billing record with them: the agreements you have signed, the messages we have sent you, and what we hold about you.
It is up to you whether you use it. You never need an account to sign a bulk-billing agreement, and nothing about your care, your appointments or your billing depends on this.
smallPrint: The link works until {{expiresOn}}. You will be asked a few details about yourself first, so that nobody else can open your record in your name.
Your AoBPlatform record ID is {{recordId}}. Every genuine message from us about your record quotes it, and you will see it on the page after you sign in.
templates.sms: {{practiceName}} has offered you a way to see your bulk-billing record with them. Open {{activationUrl}} (the link works until {{expiresOn}}). Your AoBPlatform record ID is {{recordId}}. Every genuine message from us about your record quotes it, and you will see it on the page after you sign in.

templates.note: W6, REQ-PORT-02 -- the copy the person who signed asked for on the tablet, which is the s 65C copy-on-request obligation automated. IT CARRIES A LINK, NOT THE DOCUMENT: the PDF is rendered once, deterministically, and its hash checked against the one recorded at signing before a byte is served (hard rule 13), which an attachment composed at send time could not promise. NO AMOUNT (hard rule 4) -- the agreement is an assignment of benefit and the figure is not a particular of it. NOTHING HERE SAYS ANYTHING WAS CERTIFIED OR APPROVED (hard rule 12): the sentence about the data set is the permitted form. It never asks for a reply, a detail or a confirmation -- the ceremony finished before this was sent, and nothing about care or billing waits on it (hard rule 8).
templates.subject: Your copy of the bulk-billing agreement you signed at {{practiceName}}
paragraphs: Here is your copy of the bulk-billing agreement you signed at {{practiceName}} on {{signedOn}}. Opening it needs nothing from you -- no account, no sign-in and no details.
You asked for this at the practice. There is nothing to do with it and nothing to reply to; it is yours to keep.
smallPrint: The link works until {{expiresOn}}. After that, {{practiceName}} can give you another copy at any time.
The document is checked against the s 65C data set, and the copy you open is checked against the record made when you signed it. If the two ever disagree it is not shown to you at all.
templates.sms: Your copy of the bulk-billing agreement you signed at {{practiceName}} on {{signedOn}}: {{copyUrl}} -- the link works until {{expiresOn}} and needs no sign-in. Nothing to reply to.

templates.note: TELEHEALTH-PLAN.md §3 step 5 -- the link to the one page for a telehealth consultation, sent only to the mobile or email already on the record (D-2026-09-11-03) while the provider is on the call. IT NEVER CARRIES THE CODE: the code is shown only on the provider's screen and read out on the call, which is what shows that whoever opened the link can hear the call; there is no placeholder for it and the loader refuses one. NEUTRAL UNTIL G10 IS ANSWERED: about the consultation only -- nothing about bulk billing, Medicare, the assignment or the DB4, which could make the DB4 afterwards a pre-agreement (TELEHEALTH-PLAN.md §9). It asks for nothing but the code the provider reads out.
templates.subject: Your telehealth consultation with {{practiceName}}
paragraphs: {{providerName}} at {{practiceName}} has sent you this link for your telehealth consultation.
Open it, then type the 6-digit telehealth access code {{providerName}} reads out to you on the call. The access code is never in this message.
smallPrint: If you are not on a call with {{practiceName}} right now, do nothing. The link stops working on its own.
templates.sms: {{practiceName}}: {{providerName}} sent you this link for your telehealth consultation: {{telehealthUrl}} -- type the telehealth access code {{providerName}} reads out on the call. The access code is never in this message.

templates.note: APPENDED TO THE TELEHEALTH LINK ONLY WHEN THE PROVIDER'S AHPRA REGISTRATION HAS BEEN SIGHTED AND IS CURRENT (Carl, 12 Oct 2026, D-2026-10-12-03 item 10). It tells the patient WHO their provider is and where to check it themselves; it is not offered as proof the message is genuine (anyone can quote a real number), which is the code's job. The register is named in plain text as well as linked, so a careful reader can type it rather than click. Ahpra is not Medicare: nothing here touches G10. Never the Medicare provider number, which is a billing identifier, not a public one.
paragraphs: {{providerName}} is registered with Ahpra, registration number {{ahpraNumber}}. You can check this yourself on the public register at www.ahpra.gov.au.
templates.sms: Ahpra registration {{ahpraNumber}}, check it at www.ahpra.gov.au.

templates.note: APPENDED TO EVERY TELEHEALTH LINK (Carl, 12 Oct 2026, D-2026-10-12-03 item 11). The short reference the patient quotes when they ring the practice about this consultation; the same id is at the foot of their page and beside the session on the doctor's panel, so all three can be compared. A REFERENCE, NEVER A KEY: it opens nothing, and the message never asks the patient to type it anywhere. Neutral until G10.
paragraphs: Your telehealth consultation ID is {{consultationId}}. Quote it if you call {{practiceName}} about this consultation.

templates.note: APPENDED TO EVERY PORTAL-RELATED MESSAGE, by one helper, so the sentence is identical everywhere and a patient can compare two messages and a page. Its words are the whole point: they hand the reader a rule they can apply to the NEXT message, including one we did not send.
paragraphs: Your AoBPlatform record ID is {{recordId}}. Every genuine message from us about your record quotes it, and you will see it on the page after you sign in.
